scope_note: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Switch Las Vegas NAP7, the individual real-property parcel and original SUPERNAP building at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard. The review covered Clark County assessor, Treasurer, Accela permit, planning, air-quality, budget and financial-report access points; Nevada GOED, Department of Taxation and utility-regulatory sources; Switch operator, SEC, career and ESG materials; supplier and contractor references; and recipient-reported community records for 2005-2026. Six direct observations are added without allocating wider Core Campus capital expenditure, combined incentive audits, later facilities or expansions, personal property, tenant equipment, vendor equipment, or company-wide employment to NAP7. The Treasurer record corrects the earlier research note that payment records were uncollected, but the current payment is only a partial fiscal-year amount. No synthesis fragment is added: NAP4 was already operating while NAP7 was under construction in 2008, and the available county panel cannot isolate a NAP7 treatment from earlier facilities, later Core Campus growth, or major non-data-center shocks. NAP7 employment, payroll, local supplier payments, metered electricity and water, personal-property tax, realized abatement, jurisdictional tax receipts, project-attributable public costs, and a net fiscal result remain unobserved.

project_updates.title: Chronology and building boundary verified
project_updates.notes: Clark County's September 3, 2008 rights-of-way filing identifies NAP4 as existing and NAP7 at 7135 South Decatur as under construction. The assessor's 2008 construction year and Switch's 2009 debut statement corroborate the chronology without creating a first-county-entry treatment date. The individual NAP7 building and real-property parcel remain separate from NAP8-NAP19, the Core Campus, tenant equipment, and later company-county expansion accounts. Because other Switch operations predate NAP7 and later growth overlaps the county outcome panel, no facility treatment or causal county model is added.
project_updates.project_description: Switch Las Vegas NAP7 is the original SUPERNAP colocation facility operated by Switch at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard in unincorporated Clark County, Nevada. Clark County records show NAP7 under construction in September 2008, the assessor dates the structure to 2008, and Switch reports that it debuted in 2009 with more than 400,000 square feet. This account follows the individual NAP7 building and real-property parcel while keeping adjacent Core Campus facilities, later expansions, company-county incentive accounts, tenant equipment, and other property accounts separate.

project_updates.title: Treasurer bill and partial payment correct the earlier gap
project_updates.notes: Parcel 176-01-810-001 was queried in the Clark County Treasurer portal for tax year 2027. The portal directly supports the $912,973.28 real-property bill and $228,624.01 fiscal-year payment through review, correcting the September 3 note that Treasurer payment records remained uncollected. The partial payment is not promoted to a full-year amount; calendar-year rollups, future installments, jurisdictional distributions, personal-property accounts and tax receipts remain outside these claims.

project_updates.title: Permit and contractor search found one usable remodel value
project_updates.notes: Clark Accela searches for exact NAP7 and 7135 South Decatur covered records from 2008 through 2026. The NAP7 query returned five labeled records; BD20-28271 is closed-approved and provides the distinct $200,000 interior-remodel job value. BD20-27431 was void, BD13-12024-EL3 and BD13-12024-LVSC are smaller electrical trade records with ambiguous overlap, and BD25-56296 was not complete. The 84 exact-address results include later LAS facilities, substations and unrelated campus work, so they are not attributed to NAP7. The named contractor, Switch RIG LLC, supplies identity context but no independent-vendor payment or local-retention amount.

project_updates.title: Air permit isolates NAP7 equipment but not resource use
project_updates.notes: Clark County air-quality materials for Source 16304 were searched from the 2014 authority-to-construct history through the 2025 Part 70 revision. The 2022 support document's facility table directly supports 31 permitted NAP7 emergency generators and separately lists 21 cooling towers. Permit limits, equipment ratings and potential emissions cannot establish actual runtime, diesel use, emissions, electricity load, water withdrawals, wastewater, utility bills or environmental damages; those quantities remain gaps.

project_updates.title: Incentive projections and audits remain wider than NAP7
project_updates.notes: Nevada GOED biennial reports for fiscal years 2016-2024 and state data-center abatement program pages were searched. GOED's Switch LTD #3 figures are source projections for a later Clark County expansion, not a NAP7 forecast; the audit rows combine multiple facilities and accounts. Contract labels do not establish physical NAP identity, so projected capital investment, jobs, wages and abatements and combined audit findings remain excluded from the NAP7 record set.

project_updates.title: Tax-expenditure and public-cost reports do not resolve NAP7
project_updates.notes: The Nevada Department of Taxation's 2017-18 through current tax-expenditure materials, Clark County and school-district financial reports, and state abatement disclosures were searched. State and local totals aggregate beneficiaries and do not identify NAP7, parcel 176-01-810-001 or a realized facility benefit. No facility-specific sales-tax or personal-property abatement, marginal public-service cost, infrastructure subsidy, jurisdictional receipt, or net fiscal result was found, so no public-cost or fiscal-net claim is created.

project_updates.title: Utility and water searches produced no meter-level observation
project_updates.notes: PUCN dockets and filings, NV Energy tariffs and regulatory pages, Las Vegas Valley Water District board materials, Southern Nevada Water Authority plans, and Clark County water-related searches were reviewed for Switch, NAP7, parcel 176-01-810-001 and 7135 South Decatur over 2008-2026. Public results did not disclose a NAP7 meter, peak demand, electricity consumption, bill, interconnection cost, water allocation, withdrawal, consumption, discharge or wastewater charge. Company-wide renewable-energy statements and generic data-center water testimony were not assigned to this building.

project_updates.title: Workforce, procurement and operator searches preserve facility gaps
project_updates.notes: Switch SEC filings from 2017-2022, current and archived Las Vegas facility pages, career postings, ESG reports, press releases, and contractor or equipment-provider references were searched. SEC capital expenditure remains Core Campus-wide and later-period construction largely names LAS14-LAS16 rather than NAP7. Career pages list functions and openings but not filled NAP7 jobs, resident employment, wages or payroll. APC, Cox and fiber-provider references describe equipment or connectivity roles without contract values, payment dates, local purchasing shares or a defensible NAP7 supplier-spend total; Martin-Harris references concern NAP8 and are excluded.

project_updates.title: Recipient record supports one unallocated in-kind contribution
project_updates.notes: UNLV news, foundation and supercomputing materials from 2014-2018 and Switch community and ESG materials through 2026 were searched. UNLV directly values the three-pair dark-fiber gift at $3 million, but describes connectivity to the Switch SUPERNAP colocation environment without naming NAP7, so the claim remains company-county and unallocated. Other reviewed education, museum, FIRST, sports and workforce-development references lacked amounts, dates or facility attribution; a tower donation described only as benefiting local Nevada colleges was not assigned to Clark County or NAP7.

project_updates.title: County planning and financial searches leave public-service effects unobserved
project_updates.notes: Clark County commission and Enterprise Town Advisory Board agendas, planning applications, public-works pages, annual budgets, annual comprehensive financial reports and capital plans were searched for NAP7, the parcel and exact address across 2005-2026. Results primarily concern later NAP facilities or corridor-wide works and do not quantify an NAP7-specific county expenditure, developer-funded infrastructure amount, fire or police service demand, school effect, tax distribution or service-cost offset. Later NAP17-NAP18 planning cases and broader Decatur corridor projects remain outside the selected building boundary.
